uncited: **Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel is represented by one or more geometric primitives.
**Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space.
For unit voxels, this simplifies to $P_{world} = I_{voxel} \times V_{size}$, where $V_{size}$ is the voxel dimension [S4, unofficial].
**Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized.
**Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view.

Object-order volume rendering was introduced as a fundamental technique in volume visualization, contrasting with image-order (ray casting) methods [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

The evidence in both sources explicitly defines object-order volume rendering as a technique that iterates through volumetric data samples (voxels) and projects them onto the image plane (forward mapping). Source [S1] contrasts this with image-order algorithms which use a backward mapping scheme (casting rays from pixels). Source [S2] further confirms that object-order methods process samples based on voxel organization and camera parameters, projecting them to the view plane. The claim accurately reflects these definitions and the contrast provided in the text.
